title: Prediction and validation of host cleavage targets of SARS-CoV-2 3C-like protease
authors: Yucel N; Marchiano S; Tchelepi E; Paterlini G; McAfee Q; Nimmagadda N; Ren A; Shi S; Murry C; Arany Z
one_liner_zh: 该文用生物信息算法预测SARS-CoV-2 3C样蛋白酶对宿主蛋白的切割靶点，核心是病毒蛋白酶-宿主蛋白互作，而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: How SARS-CoV-2 causes the observed range of clinical manifestations and disease severity remains poorly understood. SARS-CoV-2 encodes for two proteases (3CLPro and PLPro), vital for viral production, but also promiscuous with respect to host protein targets, likely contributing to the range of disease. Pharmacological inhibition of the 3C-like3 protease has revealed remarkable reduction in hospitalization and death in phase 2/3 clinical studies. However, the mechanisms responsible for the pathology mediated by those proteases are still unclear. In this study, we develop a bioinformatic algorithm, leveraging experimental data from SARS-CoV, to predict host cleavage targets of the SARS-CoV-2 3C-like protease, or 3CLPro. We capture targets of the 3CL protease described previously for SARS-CoV, and we identify hundreds of new putative targets. We experimentally validate a number of these predicted targets, including the giant sarcomeric protein Obscurin, and show that expression of 3CL protease alone recapitulates the sarcomeric disorganization seen by SARS-CoV-2 infection of hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. Our data provide a resource to identify putative host cleavage targets of 3CL protease that contribute to mechanisms and heterogeneity of disease in COVID-19 and future coronavirus outbreaks.
abstract_zh: SARS-CoV-2如何引起所观察到的临床表现和疾病严重程度范围，目前仍知之甚少。SARS-CoV-2编码两种蛋白酶（3CLPro和PLPro），对病毒产生至关重要，但同时也对宿主蛋白靶标具有混杂性，可能促成了疾病范围的多样性。在2/3期临床研究中，药理学抑制3C样蛋白酶已显示出住院率和死亡率的显著降低。然而，这些蛋白酶介导病理的机制仍不清楚。在本研究中，我们开发了一种生物信息学算法，利用SARS-CoV的实验数据，预测SARS-CoV-2 3C样蛋白酶（或3CLPro）的宿主切割靶标。我们捕获了先前描述的SARS-CoV 3CL蛋白酶靶标，并识别出数百个新的推定靶标。我们实验验证了其中一些预测靶标，包括巨型肌节蛋白Obscurin，并表明仅表达3CL蛋白酶即可重现SARS-CoV-2感染hiPSC来源心肌细胞所见的肌节紊乱。我们的数据提供了一个资源，用于识别3CL蛋白酶的推定宿主切割靶标，这些靶标有助于COVID-19及未来冠状病毒暴发中疾病的机制和异质性。
